description: Triggered when HTTP 5xx responses exceed the normal threshold for a service.
diagnosis_steps: Check if the error spike started after a recent deployment.
Inspect application logs for repeated exceptions or dependency failures.
Check upstream and downstream service health.
Review latency, CPU, memory, and pod restart metrics.
Verify whether the issue affects all users or a specific endpoint.
remediation_steps: Rollback the latest deployment if errors started immediately after release.
Restart unhealthy pods if they are stuck or failing readiness checks.
Scale replicas if the service is saturated.
Fail over to a healthy dependency if available.
Open an incident bridge if customer-facing impact is confirmed.

description: Triggered when payment requests time out or exceed latency thresholds.
diagnosis_steps: Check payment-service latency percentiles and timeout count.
Inspect logs for provider timeout, DB timeout, or connection pool errors.
Verify external payment provider status.
Check database connection pool utilization.
Compare timeout start time with recent deployments or traffic spikes.
remediation_steps: Restart saturated payment-service pods if connection pools are stuck.
Temporarily increase timeout only if provider latency is confirmed and business accepts delay.
Scale payment-service replicas during high traffic.
Fail over to backup payment provider if supported.
Disable duplicate retry paths until idempotency is verified.

description: Triggered when one or more pods restart frequently within a short time window.
diagnosis_steps: Run kubectl get pods and identify pods with high restart counts.
Describe affected pods and check termination reason.
Check previous container logs using kubectl logs --previous.
Review memory, CPU, liveness probe, and readiness probe metrics.
Check whether restarts began after a deployment or config change.
remediation_steps: Rollback the deployment if restarts started after a release.
Increase memory or CPU limits if resource exhaustion is confirmed.
Fix failing health probes if probe configuration is incorrect.
Restore previous ConfigMap or Secret if config parsing fails.
Create a bug ticket if application crash is reproducible.

description: Triggered when database query latency exceeds the accepted threshold.
diagnosis_steps: Identify top slow queries from database monitoring.
Check whether the slow query affects a specific table or endpoint.
Review query execution plan for full table scans.
Check DB CPU, memory, locks, and connection count.
Compare latency spike with batch jobs, deployments, or traffic changes.
remediation_steps: Add or restore missing indexes if full table scans are confirmed.
Kill long-running blocking queries if they are safe to terminate.
Scale read replicas if read traffic is high.
Temporarily disable expensive non-critical queries.
Add query regression tests for the affected endpoint.

description: Triggered when queue depth or consumer lag increases beyond threshold.
diagnosis_steps: Check current queue depth and consumer lag.
Verify whether consumers are running and healthy.
Inspect worker logs for malformed messages or processing errors.
Check dead-letter queue volume.
Compare queue growth with traffic spike or downstream dependency slowdown.
remediation_steps: Restart stuck consumers.
Scale worker replicas to increase processing throughput.
Move malformed messages to dead-letter queue.
Throttle producers if downstream systems are overloaded.
Add schema validation before messages enter the queue.

description: Triggered when cache service is unreachable or returning errors.
diagnosis_steps: Check cache instance health and connection count.
Inspect application logs for Redis connection errors.
Verify cache memory usage and eviction rate.
Check whether cache failures are causing hard application failures.
Review recent infrastructure or network changes.
remediation_steps: Fail over to cache replica if available.
Restart cache instance if it is unhealthy.
Flush only affected keys if stale data is causing incorrect behavior.
Enable graceful fallback in application if cache is non-critical.
Add circuit breaker or timeout around cache calls.

description: Triggered when TLS handshake errors increase or a certificate is expired/near expiry.
diagnosis_steps: Inspect logs for TLS handshake failure or certificate expired errors.
Check certificate expiry date for affected client or server certificate.
Verify whether the issue affects internal or external communication.
Check recent certificate rotation activity.
Confirm whether all pods loaded the new certificate.
remediation_steps: Rotate expired certificate immediately.
Restart affected pods so they reload new certificate material.
Rollback certificate change if trust chain is invalid.
Update trusted CA bundle where required.
Add certificate expiry alert at 30, 14, and 7 days before expiration.

description: Triggered when error rate increases shortly after a new deployment.
diagnosis_steps: Identify deployment version and rollout timestamp.
Compare error rate before and after deployment.
Check logs for missing environment variables, config errors, or migration failures.
Verify readiness and liveness probe status.
Check whether rollback is available and safe.
remediation_steps: Rollback to the last known good version.
Apply missing configuration if the issue is config-related.
Restart pods after configuration correction.
Pause rollout until validation passes.
Add deployment prechecks for required environment variables and config files.

description: Triggered when internal service DNS lookups fail frequently.
diagnosis_steps: Check application logs for no such host or DNS timeout errors.
Verify CoreDNS pod health and restart count.
Check CoreDNS CPU, memory, and request rate.
Test DNS resolution from an affected pod.
Review recent cluster networking or service changes.
remediation_steps: Scale CoreDNS replicas if CPU or request rate is high.
Restart unhealthy CoreDNS pods.
Check network policies blocking DNS traffic.
Reduce excessive DNS lookups using client-side caching.
Add alerting for CoreDNS saturation and DNS error rate.
evidence_to_collect: DNS test result from affected pod

description: Triggered when observability pipeline drops logs, metrics, or traces.
diagnosis_steps: Check OpenTelemetry collector logs for dropped spans or exporter queue errors.
Review collector CPU, memory, and queue utilization.
Verify backend observability platform availability.
Check whether a high-volume service started sending excessive telemetry.
Confirm exporter timeout and retry settings.
remediation_steps: Increase collector memory and CPU limits.
Tune exporter queue size and batch processor settings.
Enable sampling for high-volume traces.
Scale collector replicas.
Add alerting for telemetry drop rate and exporter queue saturation.
